title: Shuttles that weave themselves
text: Aristotle imagines tools that work on command and concludes that masters would then need no slaves: the oldest automation thought experiment.

title: Utopia's six-hour day
text: Thomas More's imagined island needs only six hours of work a day, because nobody is idle and nothing is wasted.

title: A capital grant for every 21-year-old
text: Thomas Paine proposes a national fund, paid for by a charge on inherited land, that gives each young adult a lump sum and each older person a pension: the ancestor of universal basic capital.

title: Engels' pause
text: In Britain's industrial revolution, output per worker grew much faster than real wages for two generations, and profits took a bigger share of income.

title: The Luddites
text: Textile workers smash the machines and frames they blame for cutting wages and skilled jobs.

title: The Fragment on Machines
text: Marx sketches a future in which machines, not labour time, become the main source of wealth, straining a system built on wages.

title: The Right to Be Lazy
text: Paul Lafargue argues that machines should free workers rather than lengthen their day, and that three hours of work a day would be enough.

title: Telephone operators automated
text: AT&T mechanises switching in over half its network. Incumbent operators are hurt, but later cohorts of young women find work elsewhere, including in new kinds of jobs.

title: Keynes's fifteen-hour week
text: Keynes predicts that his grandchildren will work about three hours a day, and names the transitional risk 'technological unemployment'.

title: The negative income tax
text: Milton Friedman proposes replacing a patchwork of programmes with one income floor that tapers as earnings rise.

title: The Triple Revolution memo
text: A group of activists and scholars tells President Johnson that 'cybernation' will break the link between work and income, and calls for an adequate income as a matter of right.

title: Four US income-guarantee experiments
text: Randomised negative income tax trials find work falls, modestly: on average about two weeks of full-time work a year for husbands and three for wives and single mothers.

title: Mincome, Manitoba
text: A Canadian guaranteed annual income is later linked to fewer hospitalisations and more teenagers finishing school.

title: Alaska pays its first dividend
text: Every resident receives an annual share of the Permanent Fund's oil-financed earnings, as they have every year since.

title: Leontief's horses
text: Nobel laureate Wassily Leontief warns that labour could follow the draft horse, displaced once tractors arrived.

title: '47% of jobs at risk'
text: An occupation-level model puts nearly half of US employment at high risk of computerisation; task-level studies later find far less.

title: The global labour share falls
text: Economists document a decline in labour's share of income in most countries and industries since the early 1980s.

title: Finland's basic income experiment
text: 2,000 unemployed people receive an unconditional monthly payment; employment barely moves, wellbeing improves.

title: Robots and jobs
text: US local labour markets more exposed to industrial robots lose employment and wages.

title: Generative AI spreads
text: Within two years of ChatGPT's launch, nearly 40% of US adults aged 18 to 64 use generative AI.

title: Post-Labor Economics takes shape
text: David Shapiro's 'Post AGI Economics' video starts the framework he later calls Post-Labor Economics.

title: $1,000 a month for three years
text: The largest US guaranteed-income trial finds recipients work somewhat less and take more leisure.

title: Labor/Zero
text: Shapiro launches a movement to end obligatory labour by spreading ownership, not just cash.

title: The first canaries?
text: Payroll data show young workers in the most AI-exposed jobs falling behind their peers, while aggregate employment holds up.

title: Labor Zero, the book
text: Shapiro sets out the framework in book form, with an open companion of plates, appendix and bibliography.
